# Overview

WaDorule derives reservoir-specific daily release targets from user-supplied
inflows, storage targets, elevation targets, and reservoir constraints.

The package does not contain a fixed reservoir policy or require a repository
data set. The same function can therefore be applied to different reservoirs
by changing the supplied inputs and constraints.

# Required inputs

```r
library(WaDorule)

inflows <- data.frame(
  Date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + 0:29,
  inflow = 100
)

targets <- data.frame(
  Date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + 0:29,
  Storage = 5000,
  Elevation = 300
)
```

The user also supplies the reservoir constraints:

```r
Smin <- 1000
Smax <- 10000
Rmin <- 20
Rmax <- 500
```

# Derive the release target

```r
result <- wad_wadorule(
  inflows = inflows,
  targets = targets,
  Smin = Smin,
  Smax = Smax,
  Rmin = Rmin,
  Rmax = Rmax
)

head(result)
```

The returned data frame contains:

```text
Date
Storage_Target
Elevation_Target
Release_Target
```

# Repository examples

The GitHub repository provides selected reservoir input files and generated
reference outputs. Users can download those files and run the same function
with the corresponding reservoir constraints. The reference outputs are
provided for reproduction and comparison; they are not used by the algorithm.

# Interpretation

The derived release target reflects the supplied inflow series, storage-target
trajectory, storage-level feedback, release constraints, and release-ramping
rules. Agreement or disagreement with an externally supplied or previously
generated release series should be interpreted as a comparison of operating
patterns, not as calibration or validation of the algorithm.
